newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French stocks down sharply, hit by politics.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French stocks down sharply, hit by politics.

text.p: French stocks ended the day sharply down on Friday, undermined by a bout of political worries, but the rest of Europe was lifted by a strong start on Wall Street.

The Paris bourse showed losses of 2.6 percent at the close because of uncertainty as the government let speculation spread that President Jacques Chirac may call a snap parliamentary poll for early June.

Frankfurt floor trade ended 1.15 percent down on a weaker dollar but after-hours trading on the computerised IBIS index clawed back most of the loss, comforted perhaps by Wall Street's early gains. London finished with a modest advance.
The dollar slipped over a pfennig after the German central bank President Hans Tietmeyer's comments on Thursday that the Bundesbank was not interested in seeing the mark weaken further.
The French financial markets were badly rattled as Chirac failed to quell rumours about a snap election or cabinet reshuffle, and the opposition Socialist party said it was ready to contest a vote.

The Socialists have accused Chirac of considering parliamentary elections a year early to renew the centre-right majority before a new bout of austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency.
"The rumours are such and the denials so weak that the idea has begun to sink in," said former Socialist cabinet minister Frederique Bredin.
The blue-chip CAC-40 Paris lost 67.62 points to close at 2547.56 and the franc slipped to its lowest level against the mark this month amid rumours that Chirac may make a decision at the weekend.
"Prospects of an early election drove the market down," one broker said.
Traders also said the rise on Wall Street gave no help. "This is strictly a domestic matter. New York is rising but the franc is weak. People here are focusing on politics," one dealer said.

In Frankfurt, floor trade ended down by 1.2 percent as the falling dollar dimmed exporters' prospects but computerised dealing on the IBIS index perked up to close only marginally in the minus column, down 0.6 points at 3361.2.
But volumes were thin and there was unease about volatility on Wall Street, a strong influence on European bourses.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, was the best performer, making a moderate advance after Wall Street opened with gains of 0.4 percent, led by high-tech stocks after a better-than-expected results by Microsoft.

The FTSE 100 index closed up 11.6 points at 4,310.5, for a net gain of just 39.8 points on the week as worries over the strong pound, politics, and interest rates kept many institutional investors on the sidelines.
"I'm glad this week is over. It's been a total waste of time," one senior dealer said. "The trouble is, I can't see things improving. There is just no reason to go into this market at the moment."
On currency markets, the dollar had a bad day against the mark and yen, its energy sapped by dollar-dampening comments out of Japan and Germany.

Traders said an absence of economic data from the United States and Germany was making European trade lethargic, adding that the approach of the weekend and a G7 finance ministers' meeting next week was adding to the reluctance to stir up the market.
The dollar was down over a pfennig in late trading, with sentiment uneasy because of Teitmeyer's remarks.

Against the yen, the dollar was virtually unchanged after earlier losses after remarks made overnight by Eisuke Sakakibara, the influential head of the Japanese Finance Ministry's international finance bureau.

Sakakibara, in an interview with Reuters, warned of the danger of assuming Japan would not raise interest rates within the next year. It would be natural for the Bank of Japan to raise rates when the strength of the economy was confirmed.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 1.7133 marks and 125.90 yen in late European after ending at 1.7241 and 125.97 in late trading in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 11.6 points at 4,310.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 finished down 67.62 points at 2,547.56.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 38.86 points at 3,344.39.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $342.45 an ounce versus $343.15 at the close in London on Thursday. Silver was unchanged at $4.76.
